How this manual is organised

Chapters 1 to 3 establish the common ground: purpose, architecture and security. Chapters 4 to 7 are task-oriented manuals for the four front ends. Chapters 8 to 13 cover operating discipline — administration, disaster management, backup, resilience, testing and operations. The appendices carry reference material that is consulted rather than read.

Conventions used in this manual

Procedures are numbered. Interface elements are shown in bold. Literal values, field names, environment variables and endpoints appear in monospace. Warnings describe actions that can lose or expose data; notes describe behaviour that is correct but easy to misread. Every figure and table carries a chapter-based number, and every page carries the document title and page number in the footer.

1

Part One · Introduction

Introduction

◆

What LoveLaundry is, the operation it was built for, and the vocabulary its users already speak.

1.1 Purpose

This manual documents the LoveLaundry platform: a multi-tenant operations system for a commercial laundry that also serves a retail shop counter, hotel clients, and its own linen room. It exists so that the people who run, support and extend the platform have one authoritative description of how it is put together and how it is used — not a marketing overview, and not a substitute for reading the code, but the document that makes the code and the operation legible to each other.

The manual serves three audiences at once. Operators — counter staff, supervisors, linen-room attendants, hotel front-office users — need precise, numbered procedures and a clear statement of what the system will and will not let them do. Administrators need to know how tenants, users, memberships and hotel client accounts are created, and what the security model enforces on their behalf. Engineers and support staff need the architecture, the failure modes, the recovery paths and the measured state of the test suites, so that an incident can be diagnosed without rediscovering the design under pressure.

Every statement in this manual is either derived from the implementation as it stands or is explicitly marked as a target, a policy or a recommendation. Where the platform does not yet do something, the manual says so. Chapter 12 in particular reports measured test results rather than aspirational ones, and names the gaps — no browser-driven end-to-end suite, no load testing — instead of implying coverage that does not exist.

1.2 Scope

1 · IntroductionLoveLaundry — System Manual

The manual covers the platform as deployed for a single laundry business operating four front ends against a shared service estate. The boundary is set out below so that readers know when they have left the documented surface.

In scope

  • Authentication, tenancy and membership for staff, hotel client and linen-room users.
  • Gate passes, deliveries, bills, shop bills, payments, quotations and returns.
  • Linen tagging, scanning and the full wash lifecycle, including discrepancies.
  • The monthly matrix, dispatch, dashboards and day close.
  • Deployment, configuration, backup, recovery, monitoring and incident response for the platform itself.

Out of scope

  • Accounting practice and statutory reporting outside the platform's own ledgers.
  • The internal design of third-party components (MongoDB, React, FastAPI and their dependencies).
  • Payment-provider contracts, bank settlement and card-acquirer operations.
  • Mobile client (LoveMobi) feature documentation beyond its role in the service map.
  • Hardware procurement, printer models and network cabling.
Table 1 — Scope boundaries by capability area
AreaDocumented hereBoundary note
Gate passes and deliveriesYes — fullCreation, editing, status, dispatch and the linen lines attached to each pass.
Bills and paymentsYes — fullBill generation from deliveries, payment recording, balances and day close totals.

1.3 Who the system serves

LoveLaundry is one platform with four working surfaces. Each exists because a different group of people does a different job and at a different speed. The design keeps them on one dataset while giving each a purpose-built interface.

The laundry business

The core operation: collecting soiled linen and garments by gate pass, washing and finishing them, delivering them back, and billing for the work. The laundry app (quotations-ui) is the full-surface application — gate passes, deliveries, bills, quotations, workers, reports, the monthly matrix, dispatch and day close. It is where supervisors and managers spend their day.

◆14◆
1 · IntroductionLoveLaundry — System Manual

The shop counter

A retail and walk-in service point. Customers arrive with a bag, not an account. The Shop Counter app is deliberately narrow: a today view, a bill list, a quick bill pad and a day close.

Hotel clients

Hotels are the laundry's largest customers and its most demanding readers of records. A hotel is not a separate entity in the platform: it is the client_name carried on gate passes, deliveries, bills and quotations. Hotel staff sign in with a client account and see only their own property's records — never another hotel's, and never the laundry's internal costs.

The linen room

The linen room is where physical items are counted, tagged, washed and reconciled. The Linen Room app turns that physical work into a digital trail: each tag is scanned at every stage, from collection through wash, press and readiness to delivery, with explicit actions for items that go missing, arrive damaged or are retired from service. Its users work one-handed with a scanner, so the interface is a single scan field and a short list of valid next actions.

1.4 Design principles

Seven principles explain most of the decisions in the codebase. They are stated here because they are also the grounds on which a change should be rejected.

Table 2 — Design principles and their practical consequences
PrincipleWhat it means in practice
Tenant from the tokenThe laundry_id is read from verified JWT claims. No request parameter, header or body field can set or override it. Missing context fails closed rather than falling back to an unscoped query.
One operation, one recordGate passes, deliveries and bills are separate documents with explicit links, so each can be corrected without rewriting history. A bill is derived from deliveries; it does not absorb them.
Money is additive and reversiblePayments are records, not field mutations. Balances are computed. Corrections are new records that reference the original, so an audit trail survives every mistake.
Physical truth is scannedThe linen lifecycle advances only through explicit scan actions. No status is inferred from time passing, and no bulk update silently skips a stage.
Interfaces match the jobCounter staff get speed; linen staff get one scan field; hotels get read-only clarity; managers get the full surface. No single screen tries to serve all four.
Degrade, do not disappearWhen a dependency is unavailable the affected feature stops and says so, while independent features continue. Chapter 11 states exactly what remains usable.
Recoverable by designBackups, point-in-time recovery and restore drills are part of the product, not an afterthought. Chapter 10 defines the targets and the procedure.
◆15◆
1 · IntroductionLoveLaundry — System Manual
Warning

Any change that resolves a tenant from a request body or header is a security defect, not a feature — as is any change that lets a hotel client token reach a staff endpoint.

1.5 Glossary of domain terms

The platform uses the vocabulary of the laundry trade. These terms recur throughout the manual and in the interface, and they do not always mean what a software reader would expect.

Table 3 — Core domain vocabulary
TermMeaning in LoveLaundry
Gate passThe document that accompanies goods leaving or entering the premises. It records the client, the date, the item lines and quantities, and it is the origin of every downstream delivery and bill. A gate pass is the unit of operational truth: if it is not on a pass, it did not happen.
DeliveryThe act and record of returning finished goods to the client. A delivery references the gate pass lines it fulfils, carries the delivered quantities, and is the input to billing. Partial deliveries against one pass are normal.
BillA financial document raised for one client over a period or a set of deliveries. It states quantities, rates, charges, discounts and tax, and it holds the balance outstanding. A bill is not edited once paid; corrections are made by credit or adjustment records.
Linen tagA physical label with a unique identifier attached to an item or bundle. The tag is the join between the physical item and its digital record; scanning it advances the lifecycle. Tags are printed from the Linen Room app and retired when an item leaves service.
Day closeThe end-of-day reconciliation. It freezes the day's totals — bills raised, payments received, shop sales, deliveries — and marks the business date closed so that later edits cannot silently change reported figures. Each front end has its own close, and the laundry close is the authoritative one.
Monthly matrixA grid of clients against days of the month showing daily quantities and values, used to reconcile contract volumes and to spot missing or duplicated entries. It is a reporting artefact, generated from gate passes and deliveries, not a separately maintained ledger.
QuotationA priced offer to a prospective or existing client, with line items, rates and validity. A quotation can be converted into operational work but does not itself create a bill.
Shop billA counter sale to a walk-in customer, recorded in the shop-app rather than the laundry ledger. Shop bills carry their own numbering and are reconciled at shop day close.
DispatchThe release of finished goods to the delivery route. Dispatch records who released what, to which vehicle or driver, and at what time, closing the loop between the linen room and the client.
ReturnGoods coming back from a client — rejected items, unused linen, or items sent in error. A return references the original delivery where one exists.
Client accountA login belonging to a hotel client organisation, stored in the client_accounts collection of user-service. It carries a client_scope of one laundry and one client_name; it is not a membership and grants no staff capability.
Tenant / laundryThe laundry business that owns a set of records. Represented by laundry_id. Every business document carries it and every query filters on it.
MembershipThe link between a user and a laundry, carrying the user's role in that laundry. A user may hold memberships in more than one laundry; each session acts in exactly one.
CapabilityA named permission such as bill:write or linen:scan. Roles are bundles of capabilities; endpoints check capabilities, not role names.
DiscrepancyA mismatch between expected and scanned linen quantities or statuses. Discrepancies are recorded, not corrected silently, so that loss patterns remain visible.
◆16◆
1 · IntroductionLoveLaundry — System Manual
Note on “hotel”

Throughout this manual, “hotel” refers to a client organisation identified by the client_name string. It is never a database entity, never a tenant, and never a login domain of its own. Chapter 2.8 explains why this matters for isolation.

Part One · System Overview and Architecture

System Overview and Architecture

◆

Six services, four front ends, three databases, one tenancy rule.

2.1 Service map

LoveLaundry is a service-oriented system built from Python/FastAPI services, each owning a bounded part of the business, behind four React front ends. There is no shared application server and no shared in-process state: a front end calls a service over HTTPS with a bearer token, and the service answers from the database it owns. Figure 1 shows the estate as deployed.

2 · System Overview and ArchitectureLoveLaundry — System Manual
Why this shape

The split follows ownership, not technology. Identity and tenancy change rarely and must be trusted by everyone, so they live in user-service. Operational documents change constantly and are read by all four front ends, so they live in bill_service. Accounting follows its own reporting calendar and retention rules, so it is isolated in laundry-management.

2.2 Service catalogue

Each service is independently deployable and owns its collections. The table below is the authoritative list of services, their responsibilities and their development ports.

◆19◆
2 · System Overview and ArchitectureLoveLaundry — System Manual
Table 4 — Services, responsibilities and interfaces
ServicePortResponsibilityOwns
user-service8002Authentication for staff and hotel clients, user records, laundries (tenants), memberships, hotel client accounts, role and capability resolution, token issuance.users, laundries, memberships, client_accounts
bill_service8001The operational core: gate passes, deliveries, bills, shop bills, linens and tag lifecycles, returns, monthly matrix, dispatch, day close and dashboards.Operational collections in the operations database
laundry-management—Accounting: customers, transactions, payments, expenses, salary, employees and priced items. Feeds financial reporting and the payment ledger.Accounting database
quotation-service—Quotation drafting, pricing line items and the AI chat surface used to assemble offers.Quotation collections
worker-service—Worker records, assignment and attendance. Supplies worker lists to the laundry app.Worker collections
love-ai—AI assistance: drafting, summarisation and conversational help over permitted data. Invoked by the other services and by the laundry app.No business data of record

Division of responsibility

user-service is the only issuer of tokens and the only authority on who a caller is. It answers three questions for every other service: is this token genuine, which laundry is this session acting in, and what may this caller do. It stores the membership snapshot that is copied into the token, so downstream services do not need a database lookup to resolve tenancy.

bill_service is where the business actually happens. Gate passes are created here, linen lines are attached here, deliveries are recorded here, and bills are raised here. It is also the service the shop counter and hotel desk call, and the one that must remain available for the business to trade.

laundry-management holds the money in its accounting form: customers, transactions, payments, expenses, salaries, employees and items. It is separate from the operational ledger because accounting records have different retention, correction rules and audience. A payment recorded operationally is mirrored into accounting, never edited in place in either system.

quotation-service owns the pre-sale conversation. A quotation is a priced proposal with line items and validity; it can become work, but it never becomes a bill by itself. worker-service owns people and attendance. love-ai holds no data of record: it reads through the services that do, and anything it drafts must be saved through a normal write path with a normal capability check.

Ports and addressing

The ports above are development defaults. In a deployed environment the reverse proxy terminates TLS and routes by path prefix, and the services listen on the loopback interface only. A service port is never published to the internet, and no front end hard-codes one: service base URLs are supplied at build time through Vite environment variables.

2.3 Front-end applications

Four React applications share a toolchain and a design language but not a codebase. Each is built with React 19, TypeScript, Vite 8 and Tailwind CSS 4, and each is deployed as static assets behind the same reverse proxy. Two additional surfaces — the guest-billing print view and the public marketing site — are served alongside them.

Shared conventions

◆21◆
2 · System Overview and ArchitectureLoveLaundry — System Manual
  • Session storage. Each application stores its token under its own key — ll_shop_session, ll_hotel_session, ll_linen_session — so that two applications open in the same browser cannot overwrite each other's session, and so that a token issued to one audience is never silently reused by another.
  • Token in the header. Every request attaches Authorization: Bearer <token>. No application puts a token in a query string, and none stores a token in a cookie readable by scripting.
  • No client-side authorisation. Buttons are hidden when a capability is absent, but the check that matters is on the server. Hiding a control is a usability measure, not a security control.
  • Fail visible. When a call fails with 401 the application clears its session and returns to sign-in; when it fails with 403 it shows a permission message and leaves the session intact; when it fails with 5xx it shows a retry affordance and does not silently retry a write.

Build and release

Each application builds to a static bundle with vite build and is served from the reverse proxy under its own path. Build-time configuration is injected through Vite environment variables (VITE_*), which means an artefact is environment-specific: the same commit built for staging and for production produces different bundles. Release therefore always involves a build, never a file copy between environments.

Note

The three new applications — shop-app, hotel-app and linen-room-app — share a common scaffolding and authentication pattern but are separate deployments. A defect in one does not take down the others, and an upgrade can be rolled out one counter at a time.

Table 7 — Front-end toolchain
ConcernChoice
UI libraryReact 19 with function components and hooks
LanguageTypeScript, strict mode
Build toolVite 8 — development server with HMR, production static bundle
StylingTailwind CSS 4 with a shared colour and spacing token set

2.4 Request lifecycle

Every authenticated request follows the same seven-stage path. The order matters: identity is established before tenancy, tenancy before authorisation, and authorisation before any database access. A request that fails at any stage never reaches the next one.

◆22◆
2 · System Overview and ArchitectureLoveLaundry — System Manual
Table 8 — Stage-by-stage failure behaviour
StageEnforced byOn failure
1 RequestClient HTTP wrapperNo token → the app redirects to sign-in without calling the API.
2 EdgeReverse proxyOversized body → 413; TLS failure → connection refused; timeout → 504.
3 VerifyAuth middlewareBad signature, expired token or wrong token_kind → 401 with a generic message.
4 TenancyTenant dependencyNo laundry_id in claims → 403. There is no unscoped fallback and no default tenant.
5 AuthoriseCapability dependencyCapability not held for this laundry → 403, logged with the capability name.
6 ExecuteRepository layerCross-tenant reference, stale version or duplicate key → 409 or 422; nothing is written.
7 RespondSerialiser and loggerSerialisation error → 500 with a request id; the audit entry records the failure.

The practical consequence is that a handler never has to ask “which laundry is this?”. It receives a resolved tenant context, or it is never called. That single decision removes an entire class of defect — the query that forgets its filter — because there is no filter to forget: the repository takes the tenant as a mandatory argument.

2.5 The three-database model

The platform separates its data into three MongoDB databases along ownership lines. The split is not cosmetic: it constrains what each service can see, it lets each store be backed up and restored on its own schedule, and it keeps a reporting query from ever competing with a counter sale for the same lock or connection pool.

Identity and tenancy — user_db

Holds users, laundries, memberships and client_accounts. It is small, changes rarely, and is read on every sign-in. Its integrity is a precondition for everything else: if identity is wrong, every downstream decision is wrong. It is written only by user-service.

Operations — the bill_service database

Holds gate_passes, deliveries, bills, shop_bills, linens, returns, day-close records, dispatch records and the materialised monthly matrix. This is the largest and busiest store, written by every front end and read by dashboards, and it is the one whose loss stops the business trading.

◆23◆
2 · System Overview and ArchitectureLoveLaundry — System Manual

Accounting — laundry-management

Holds customers, transactions, payments, expenses, employees, items and salary records. It follows accounting conventions: records are posted, not edited; periods are closed; and the ledger is the source of financial truth even when an operational figure disagrees.

Rules that hold the model together

  • One writer per collection. A service writes only its own collections. There is no shared collection and no “just this once” cross-write, because the second writer is always the one that skips a validation.
  • No cross-database joins. Where a document needs data from another domain, it stores the identifier and the small denormalised fragment it needs at write time — a client name, a rate, a worker name — and treats that fragment as a snapshot, not a live reference.
  • References are validated at the boundary. Creating a delivery that references a gate pass checks that the pass exists in the same tenant; a valid identifier from another laundry is rejected exactly like a fabricated one.
  • Restore order is fixed. user_db first, operations second, accounting third — because operations records reference identity and accounting records reference operations. Chapter 10 uses this order in every restore procedure.
  • Backups are per database. Each store has its own RPO and retention, reflecting how much history each one must be able to reconstruct.

Why not one database?

A single database would be simpler to operate and harder to reason about. Three concerns drive the separation. First, blast radius: a runaway reporting aggregation in the operations store must not degrade sign-in. Second, retention: accounting records must survive longer and be restorable to a specific date without replaying operational churn. Third, authority: when an operational balance and an accounting balance disagree, the platform needs an unambiguous rule about which one is corrected — and that rule is only credible if the two live in different stores.

Note

The three databases may run on the same MongoDB replica set in a small deployment. Separation is logical first and physical second; the ownership rules apply either way, and a future move to separate clusters requires no application change.

StoreWrite rateGrowth driverRestore priorityLoss impact
user_dbLowUsers and memberships1 — firstNobody can sign in; total outage
OperationsHighDaily passes, deliveries, scans2 — secondTrading stops; unbilled work
AccountingMediumTransactions and payroll3 — thirdReporting and settlement impaired

Denormalisation, and why it is deliberate

Operational documents copy small fragments of other domains at write time: a gate pass stores the client_name string, a delivery line stores the item description and rate, a bill stores the client's billing name. This is not a violation of ownership: it is how the platform avoids cross-database joins and keeps historical documents readable after the source record changes.

The rule is that a copied fragment is a snapshot of what was true when the document was written. Renaming a client does not rewrite last month's invoices; it changes what future documents carry. The same applies to rates: a bill raised at an old rate remains correct at that rate, and a re-price is a new document, not an edit.

◆25◆
2 · System Overview and ArchitectureLoveLaundry — System Manual

What each service may read

  • A service reads its own collections freely, always with the tenant filter applied.
  • A service reads another domain's data only through that domain's HTTP interface, with the caller's own token.
  • Reporting reads are the exception that proves the rule: dashboards and the monthly matrix are computed inside bill_service from its own collections, not by reaching into accounting.
Warning

A direct database read across domains — for example, joining bills to payments inside a single aggregation — couples two services' schemas and breaks the restore-order guarantees in Chapter 10. Use the owning service's API.

2.7 JWT and tenancy flow

Tenancy is established once, at sign-in, and carried in the token thereafter. The sequence below shows a staff sign-in and the first authenticated read that follows it.

What the token is, and is not

◆26◆
2 · System Overview and ArchitectureLoveLaundry — System Manual

The token is a signed statement of identity, tenant and capability. It is not a session record: the services keep no session table, which is why a stolen token remains usable until it expires and why expiry is kept short — 24 hours for staff, 12 hours for hotel clients. Revocation is therefore a matter of disabling the user or the client account and rotating the signing key, not of deleting a row; Chapter 3.6 describes the procedure.

The laundries claim is a snapshot of the user's memberships at sign-in. It exists so that downstream services can resolve a laundry name without calling user-service, and so that a session can switch tenants only by signing in again — which is the intended behaviour, because a silent tenant switch is exactly the mistake the design is trying to prevent.

Note

A user with memberships in two laundries has two valid tenants, but a token names exactly one. Switching laundry re-authenticates. This is a deliberate trade of convenience for certainty.

2.8 Hotel client-account isolation

Hotels are the platform's most sensitive external readers, and the design that protects them is deliberately unusual. A hotel is not an entity. There is no hotels collection and no hotel tenant. A hotel is the client_name string carried on gate passes, deliveries, bills and quotations — a value that already existed in the operational data before the hotel portal was built.

Hotel logins live in a separate client_accounts collection in user-service. A client account records an email, a password hash, a status, the laundry it belongs to and the client_name it may see. It holds no role, no membership and no capability list, because a hotel user is not staff and must never be granted a staff permission by accident.

How the isolation actually works

When a hotel signs in through POST /client/auth/login, user-service issues a token with a deliberately different shape. It carries no laundry_id and no laundries claim. Instead it carries:

{
  "sub": "<client account id>",
  "token_kind": "client",
  "client_scope": { "laundry_id": "<tenant>", "client_name": "<hotel name>" },
  "exp": <issued + 12 hours>
}

Staff endpoints resolve the tenant from laundry_id or from the laundries membership snapshot. A client token has neither, so those endpoints reject it automatically — not because someone remembered to add a check, but because the tenant dependency cannot resolve a context and therefore fails closed. There is no path by which a hotel token can reach a staff handler and be treated as a member of staff.

Hotel portal endpoints live under /client-portal and read client_scope explicitly. Every query filters on both laundry_id and client_name. Filtering on the name alone would be unsafe — two laundries could serve hotels with the same name — and filtering on the laundry alone would expose every hotel's data to every other hotel. Requiring both makes the pair the effective scope.

◆27◆
2 · System Overview and ArchitectureLoveLaundry — System Manual
Table 11 — Token shapes compared
ClaimStaff tokenHotel client token
token_kind"staff""client"
laundry_idPresent — the active tenantAbsent by design
laundriesMembership snapshot with rolesAbsent by design
client_scopeAbsent{ laundry_id, client_name }
role / capabilitiesRole plus resolved capability listNone — portal endpoints check scope only
Lifetime24 hours12 hours
Accepted byStaff routes on all services/client-portal routes only
Rejected by/client-portal routesEvery staff route, automatically

Why not give hotels a tenant?

Making a hotel a tenant would multiply the identity surface: every hotel would need a laundry, a membership, a role and a capability set, and every operational query would need a second scoping rule to decide whether the caller was staff or client. It would also make the existing data wrong, because the operational documents already carry client_name and no hotel identifier.

The chosen design keeps one tenant per laundry and one extra dimension — client_name — that is already present in the data. The cost is that hotel accounts are managed separately from staff accounts, which Chapter 8.3 covers. The benefit is that the two classes of token cannot be confused, and that a defect in hotel-facing code cannot escalate into staff authority.

Warning

Adding laundry_id to a client token to “simplify” a query destroys this isolation: the token would then satisfy the staff tenant dependency. Hotel portal code must read client_scope, never a top-level tenant claim.

2.9 Deployment topology

The reference deployment is a single application host behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy, with MongoDB on a separate host and backups written to object storage. This is the topology the recovery procedures in Chapter 10 assume.

◆28◆
2 · System Overview and ArchitectureLoveLaundry — System Manual

Operating assumptions

  • Single application host. The reference deployment accepts a single host as a single point of failure for compute, mitigated by documented rebuild steps and by the fact that all state lives in MongoDB and object storage.
  • MongoDB replica set. Three members are recommended: one primary, one secondary for failover, and one arbiter or a third data-bearing member. The oplog is what makes point-in-time recovery possible.
  • Backups off-host. Backup files are written to an object-storage bucket in a separate account with immutability enabled, so that a compromised application host cannot delete its own history.
  • Static assets are disposable. Front-end bundles can be rebuilt from source at any time; they are not backed up as data, only as release artefacts.

2.10 Technology stack

The stack is deliberately conventional. Every component is widely used, well documented and replaceable, because a laundry platform is maintained by a small team and must remain legible to whoever inherits it.

Version policy

Front-end dependencies are pinned in the lockfile and upgraded deliberately, one minor version at a time, with a build and a smoke test after each step. Major upgrades — such as the move to React 19 and Tailwind 4 — are treated as projects: they are scheduled, tested against the four applications and released together, because a split across applications would leave staff switching between two visual languages.

Python service dependencies are pinned in the requirements file per service. A service may be upgraded independently, which is one of the practical benefits of the split: bill_service can stay on a proven dependency set while a lower-risk service takes a newer one.

What the stack deliberately excludes

  • No client-side database. The applications cache responses for resilience (Chapter 11.4) but never treat the cache as a source of truth.
  • No message broker in the reference deployment. Cross-service side effects use durable outbox records and retries rather than introducing an operational dependency the team would have to run.
  • No server-side rendering. The applications are internal tools behind authentication; search-engine visibility is irrelevant and a static bundle is simpler to secure.
  • No micro-front-end framework. Four separate deployments achieve independence without a runtime composition layer.

2.11 · Service dependencies

Service dependency graph

Which service calls which, and what fails when an arrow breaks.

The graph is deliberately shallow. Clients talk to services; services talk to user-service for identity and to each other only where a business operation genuinely spans two domains. There is no service that every other service depends on except the identity authority, and that is the single point the platform accepts.

Reading the graph during an incident is a matter of following the arrows backwards from the symptom. A shop counter that cannot take payment is not a shop problem: the arrow from shop-app to bill_service is broken, and the first question is whether bill_service is reachable or merely slow.

◆31◆
2 · System Overview and ArchitectureLoveLaundry — System Manual

2.12 · Tenancy decision flow

Tenancy decision flow

Five checks, in order, before a single document is read.

Chapter 3 sets out the enforcement rules in full from page 34. Tenancy is not a filter applied at the end of a query; it is a sequence of decisions that must all succeed before a query is built. The order matters: identity before token kind, token kind before tenant, tenant before membership, membership before the record itself.

The practical consequence is that a handler never asks which laundry is calling. It receives a resolved tenant context or it is never invoked, which removes the class of defect in which a developer forgets a filter.

Rule

A refusal never distinguishes a foreign record from a missing one. Both return not-found, so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate another tenant's documents.

2.13 · Failure domains

Deployment topology and failure domains

What fails together, and why the backup must live outside the blast radius.

◆32◆
2 · System Overview and ArchitectureLoveLaundry — System Manual

The topology is drawn as three domains rather than three tiers, because the question that matters in a disaster is not what talks to what but what disappears together. The application host is disposable: it holds no state and can be rebuilt from the deployment steps.

The database is the domain that stops trade, and object storage is the domain that makes recovery possible. Keeping them in separate accounts is the control that prevents one compromised credential from removing both the data and its history.

Rule

If the database and its backups share an account, ransomware has one target, not two. Separation of accounts is a recovery control, not an administrative preference.

◆33◆
3

Part One · Security Model

Security Model

◆

Who can sign in, what they may do, and why one laundry can never read another's records.

3.1 Authentication

The platform recognises three kinds of principal, and each has its own sign-in path. Staff — owners, managers, supervisors and counter staff — sign in against user-service with an email and password and receive a 24-hour staff token. Linen-room staff use the same path with linen-room roles attached to their membership. Hotel clients sign in against a separate endpoint with a separate collection and receive a 12-hour client token with a different claim shape. There is no anonymous access to any business endpoint.

Table 14 — Authentication paths
PrincipalEndpointLifetimeToken characteristics
Staff (laundry app, shop)POST /auth/login24 hourstoken_kind: "staff", laundry_id, laundries snapshot, role and capabilities
Linen-room staffPOST /auth/login24 hoursSame as staff, with LINEN_SUPERVISOR or HOUSEKEEPER role and linen capabilities
Hotel clientPOST /client/auth/login12 hourstoken_kind: "client", client_scope, no tenant claim, no capabilities

Credential handling

3 · Security ModelLoveLaundry — System Manual
  • Passwords are never stored. Only a salted, slow hash is persisted. The plaintext exists for the duration of the request and is never logged, echoed or written to an audit record.
  • Sign-in responses are deliberately uniform. A wrong password and an unknown email produce the same message and the same shape of failure, so that the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate accounts.
  • Status is checked at sign-in and at use. A disabled user or client account cannot obtain a token; a token already issued for an account that is later disabled is rejected once the account status cache is refreshed, and immediately on the next sign-in attempt.
  • Tenant is chosen at sign-in. If a user holds memberships in more than one laundry, the session is bound to one. Switching requires re-authentication — there is no endpoint that changes laundry_id inside a live token.
  • Client accounts cannot be promoted. There is no code path that converts a client_accounts record into a membership, and no endpoint that issues a staff token for a client account.

Session handling in the front ends

Each application keeps its token under its own key: ll_shop_session for the shop, ll_hotel_session for the hotel desk and ll_linen_session for the linen room. Separate keys mean that a supervisor who opens the shop app and the linen app in the same browser holds two independent sessions and cannot accidentally act in the wrong one. On a 401 the application clears its own key and returns to sign-in; it does not retry with the same token and it does not fall back to another stored session.

Warning

Token lifetime is a security control, not a convenience setting. Extending the staff lifetime to “avoid signing in every morning” lengthens the window in which a stolen token is usable, because there is no server-side session to revoke. Disable the account or rotate the signing key instead.

What authentication does not do

Authentication establishes who is calling. It does not establish what they may do — that is authorisation, covered next — and it does not by itself confine them to a tenant, which is why the tenant dependency runs as a separate stage and fails closed. A valid token with no resolvable tenant is useless: it authenticates a caller the platform then refuses to serve.

3.2 Roles and capabilities

Authorisation is capability-based. A role is a named bundle of capabilities, and every protected endpoint declares the capability it requires. Adding a role means adding a bundle; it never means adding an if role == … branch inside a handler. The complete matrix is in Appendix B; this section explains the roles and the reasoning behind the bundles.

Why capabilities rather than roles in code

Role names are a poor thing to check inside a handler, because the business will always want one more variation — a senior housekeeper who may retire items, a counter supervisor who may post payments. With capabilities, that variation is a bundle change in one place, and the audit answer is a capability the user held rather than a job title interpreted somewhere in code.

3.3 Tenant isolation rules

Tenant isolation is the single most important property of the platform, and it is enforced by construction rather than by discipline. The rules below are stated as invariants: each one is either true of every request or the request fails.

Table 17 — Tenancy invariants
#InvariantHow it is enforced
1The tenant is read only from verified JWT claims.Tenant dependency reads laundry_id from the decoded token. No request field is consulted for tenancy.
2Every query carries the tenant filter.Repositories take the tenant as a required argument; there is no repository method that omits it.
3A missing tenant fails closed.No claim → 403 before any handler runs. There is no default tenant and no unscoped fallback.
4Cross-tenant references are rejected.Creating a delivery against a gate pass from another laundry returns 404 or 422 — the referenced document is treated as non-existent.
5Identifier lookups are tenant-scoped.A valid identifier from another tenant behaves exactly like a fabricated one; the query never runs without the filter.
6Aggregations and reports are scoped.Dashboard and matrix pipelines begin with a $match on laundry_id, never with a global scan.
7Hotel reads require both keys./client-portal queries filter on laundry_id and client_name from client_scope.
8Staff routes reject client tokens.Client tokens carry no laundry_id and no laundries claim, so the tenant dependency cannot resolve and the request fails.

How a violation surfaces

The platform deliberately does not distinguish “this record belongs to someone else” from “this record does not exist”. Both produce the same 404 or 422. The reason is that a different response would confirm the existence of another tenant's data, which is itself a leak: an attacker could enumerate identifiers and learn how many gate passes a competitor processes.

At the query level the filter is not applied as a post-processing step. A request for /gatepasses/{id} compiles to a lookup on { _id: id, laundry_id: <claim> }. If the identifier exists in another tenant, the query returns nothing, the handler raises not-found, and no document is ever loaded into memory.

Where tenancy is checked, end to end

◆37◆
3 · Security ModelLoveLaundry — System Manual
  • At sign-in: user-service resolves memberships and refuses to issue a token for a laundry the user does not belong to.
  • On every request: the tenant dependency extracts and validates the claim, then exposes a tenant context object to the handler.
  • In every repository call: the tenant is part of the query signature, so a handler cannot call a data access method without supplying it.
  • In every write: new documents have laundry_id stamped from the context, never from the payload. A payload that includes laundry_id is rejected rather than trusted.
  • In cross-domain calls: the caller's token is forwarded, so the callee applies the same claim and cannot be tricked into a wider scope.

Testing the invariant

Tenancy is covered by explicit tests in both service suites: a request without a tenant claim must fail, a request with a foreign identifier must return not-found, a payload carrying laundry_id must be rejected, and a client token must be refused by staff routes. These are regression tests, not exploratory ones — they exist because the invariant is the product's central promise, and a refactor that quietly weakens it would otherwise pass every functional test.

Warning

Never add a “system” or “service” flag that skips the tenant dependency. If an internal job needs cross-tenant access, it must iterate tenants explicitly, one scoped operation at a time, so that each unit of work has a named tenant in its logs.

3.4 Encryption at rest

Sensitive fields are encrypted before they reach MongoDB, using envelope encryption with AES-256-GCM. The database stores ciphertext, an initialisation vector and an authentication tag; it never stores the key that could decrypt them. The design has three parts: a per-document data key, a key-encryption key that wraps it, and a deterministic search token that allows equality lookups without decryption.

◆38◆
3 · Security ModelLoveLaundry — System Manual

The three parts

Per-document data key. Each document that contains sensitive fields gets its own 256-bit data encryption key. The key is used once to encrypt the sensitive values with AES-256-GCM, a fresh 96-bit initialisation vector per encryption, and the resulting authentication tag is stored with the ciphertext. Reading the document requires the tag to verify; a tampered field fails rather than returning plausible garbage.

Key-encryption key. The data keys are themselves encrypted — wrapped — by a key-encryption key that is held outside the database, in the environment's key store or secret manager. The database therefore contains wrapped keys that are useless without the KEK. A stolen database backup yields ciphertext and wrapped keys, not plaintext.

Search tokens. Encrypted values cannot be matched with a $regex or a range query, and the platform does not pretend otherwise. Where equality lookup is required — a client name, an account reference — the service also stores an HMAC-SHA256 token computed with a tenant-scoped search key. Queries match the token, never the ciphertext. Because the input space of names is small, a plain hash would be reversible by dictionary attack; an HMAC with a secret key is not.

What is encrypted, and what is not

Encryption is applied to personal and commercial identifiers: client contact details, addresses, account references and free-text notes that may contain personal data. Operational keys — identifiers, dates, statuses, quantities and amounts — remain in clear because they are required for indexing, sorting, aggregation and reconciliation, and because encrypting them would make the monthly matrix impossible without decrypting every document in memory. The boundary is deliberate and documented so that a future reviewer does not assume more protection than exists.

Key custody

Losing the KEK loses the encrypted fields permanently; there is no recovery path by design. The KEK is therefore backed up separately from the database, under a different access policy, and its escrow is tested in the restore drill described in Chapter 10.7.

◆39◆
3 · Security ModelLoveLaundry — System Manual

3.5 Transport, audit and rate limiting

Transport

All traffic between clients and services, and between services and MongoDB, is encrypted in transit. The reverse proxy terminates TLS 1.2 or 1.3 with modern cipher suites, redirects plain HTTP to HTTPS, and sets HTTP Strict Transport Security so that a browser refuses to downgrade on subsequent visits. Certificates are issued for the platform's hostnames and renewed automatically; expiry is monitored as an alert.

Internal calls stay inside the private network and are authenticated with the caller's token. MongoDB connections use TLS with a per-service credential, so a service can read only the database it owns. The only public listener is the proxy on port 443.

Audit

Security-relevant events are recorded with the actor, the tenant, the action, the target and the outcome. Audit records are append-only and are written even when the action fails, because a rejected attempt is often more interesting than a successful one.

Table 18 — Audited events
Event classRecorded detail
Sign-in success and failureEmail, tenant where resolvable, source address, user agent, outcome. Failures never include the submitted password.
Token rejectionReason class only — expired, bad signature, wrong token kind, unresolvable tenant — with the route and request id.
Authorisation denialRequired capability, the caller's role, the route, the tenant.
Privileged writesUser creation, role change, membership change, client account creation or status change, day close, bill issue, payment post and reversal.
Data correctionAmendment of a delivery, cancellation of a gate pass, adjustment of a bill — with reason and before/after summary.
Administrative accessBackup restore, key rotation, environment change, tenant creation.

Audit entries are structured JSON written to the log pipeline with a retention period longer than the operational data they describe. They are not editable through any application route: no endpoint updates or deletes an audit record, and the application's storage credential is append-only.

Rate limiting

Rate limits protect the sign-in endpoints from credential stuffing and the write endpoints from runaway clients — a scanner stuck in a retry loop, or a page that resubmits a bill. Limits are applied per source address and per account at the proxy and again in the service, so that a misconfigured proxy does not remove the protection.

◆40◆
3 · Security ModelLoveLaundry — System Manual
Table 19 — Rate-limit classes
ClassApplies toBehaviour on breach
Authentication/auth/login, /client/auth/login429 with a retry hint; repeated breaches escalate to a temporary block and an alert
ReadList and detail routes429; clients back off with jitter
WriteCreates, updates, payments429 before the handler; no partial write occurs
ScanLinen scan submissionsBurst allowance for rapid scanning, then 429 with the remaining budget reported
Export and reportMonthly matrix, statements, PDF generationQueued rather than rejected where the operation is long-running

Thresholds are configuration values rather than code constants, so that a busy Saturday can be accommodated without a deployment. They are recorded with the rest of the environment configuration in Chapter 8.4, and any change to them is an audited administrative action.

Warning

Rate limiting is not a substitute for authorisation. A caller who is under the limit and holds the wrong capability must still be refused; the two controls answer different questions.

3.6 Secrets management

The platform depends on a few high-value secrets: the JWT signing key, the key-encryption key, the search key for HMAC tokens, database credentials for each service, and the object-storage credential used by backups.

Rules

  • No secret in source control. Configuration files in the repository contain placeholders only. A committed secret is treated as compromised and rotated, even if the commit is reverted.
  • No secret in a front-end bundle. Vite exposes every VITE_* variable to the browser.
  • One credential per service. Each service has its own database user, limited to its own database. bill_service cannot authenticate against the accounting database, which converts a service compromise into a bounded incident.
  • Secrets are injected at start-up. They arrive from the environment or a secret manager, never from a file inside the deployment directory, and they are never written to logs.
  • Redaction is default. The logging configuration redacts authorization, password, token, secret and cookie at any depth, so a careless log.info(payload) cannot leak a credential.
  • Rotation is scheduled and tested. Signing keys and database credentials rotate on a defined calendar (Chapter 13.4); the rotation procedure is exercised before it is needed.

Rotating the JWT signing key

Because tokens are stateless, rotation must be staged so that valid sessions are not all terminated at once — unless termination is the intent.

◆41◆
3 · Security ModelLoveLaundry — System Manual
  1. Generate the new key and add it to the key set as the next signing key, keeping the current key for verification.
  2. Deploy the updated key set to every service. Verification now accepts both keys; signing still uses the old key.
  3. Confirm that all services report the new key set version — a service that missed the deployment will reject newly signed tokens.
  4. Switch signing to the new key. Existing sessions continue to verify against the old key until they expire.
  5. After the longest token lifetime has elapsed (24 hours for staff), remove the old key from the set.
  6. Record the rotation in the audit log with the operator, the time and the key identifier.
Emergency rotation

If a signing key is believed compromised, skip the staged overlap: remove the old key immediately, accepting that every session is invalidated and every user must sign in again. A forced sign-in is a minor inconvenience; an attacker minting staff tokens is a Severity 1 incident.

Rotating the KEK and search key

The KEK is rotated by introducing a new key identifier and re-wrapping each document's data key with it. Documents are not re-encrypted, so the operation is fast and can run in the background; each document records the key_id of the KEK that wrapped its DEK, which makes the migration resumable and safe to interrupt. The old KEK is retained until every document reports the new identifier, then retired.

The search key is harder to rotate because its output is stored: changing the key invalidates every existing token. Rotation therefore requires a backfill that recomputes tokens for all affected documents, performed during a maintenance window with writes paused for the affected collection. Chapter 13.4 schedules this annually rather than continuously, because the cost is real and the benefit is marginal unless the key is suspected compromised.

Response to a suspected secret leak

  1. Identify which secret is exposed and what it grants: a signing key forges sessions; a database credential reads a database; a storage credential reads or deletes backups.
  2. Revoke or rotate the secret first, then investigate. Containment precedes understanding.
  3. Preserve evidence: snapshot logs and audit records before rotating, because rotation may invalidate the trail's context.
  4. Determine the exposure window and the records touched, using audit entries and database access logs.
  5. Notify according to Chapter 9.6 if personal data may have been accessed.
  6. Record the incident and the rotation in the post-incident review, and add a control that would have prevented it.

3.7 · Token shapes compared

Token shapes compared

Two kinds of session, deliberately unequal.

◆42◆
3 · Security ModelLoveLaundry — System Manual

The two tokens are not variants of one design; they are different instruments. A staff token asserts a person, a tenant and a set of capabilities. A client token asserts a property and a scope, and nothing else — no tenant claim, no role, no capability list.

The asymmetry is what makes the isolation automatic. Staff endpoints resolve a tenant from the token, so a token without one cannot pass, no matter which route it is sent to. Hotel endpoints read the scope object, so a staff token cannot satisfy them either.

Rule

Adding a tenant claim to a client token to simplify a query would collapse the distinction and let a hotel satisfy a staff authorisation check. The absence is the control.

Part Two · User Manual — Laundry App

User Manual — Laundry App

◆

The full-surface application for the laundry business: passes, deliveries, bills, quotations, workers, reports and day close.

4.1 Sign-in

The laundry app is the quotations-ui application, extended for the operational modules. It is the only surface that exposes the complete commercial picture, and therefore the only one where a manager can move from a gate pass to the bill it produced and the payment that settled it.

Procedure — signing in

4 · User Manual — Laundry AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
  1. Open the laundry app in a supported browser on a device you control.
  2. Enter your account email. Use your own account: the audit trail, and therefore every correction you make, is attributed to it.
  3. Enter your password and select Sign in.
  4. If you hold memberships in more than one laundry, choose the laundry you are working in for this session. The choice is bound to the session and cannot be changed without signing in again.
  5. Confirm the laundry name shown in the top bar matches the business you are working for before entering any data.
Note

Sign-in failures do not distinguish between a wrong password and an unknown account. This is deliberate: a different message would let an outsider discover which email addresses have accounts.

4.2 Dashboards

The dashboard answers one question: what needs attention today? It is not a reporting surface — reports live under Reports — and it is not a workflow queue. Every tile is either a count that should be driven to zero, or a total that should match a physical count.

Table 20 — Dashboard tiles and what each one means
TileMeaning and expected action
Open gate passesPasses received but not yet fully delivered. A number that only grows means deliveries are not being recorded, not that work is piling up.
Due todayPasses whose promised return date is today. Work these first; the tile turns amber when any item is overdue.
Ready for deliveryItems washed, pressed and marked ready in the linen room. These are physically on the rack and should leave today.
Unbilled deliveriesDeliveries recorded but not yet included in a bill. The figure should be zero at day close; anything left is revenue at risk.
Outstanding balanceSum of unpaid balances across clients for the current period. Drill through to the client list, then to the bill.
Linen discrepanciesOpen missing or damaged records. These need a supervisor decision, not a silent write-off.
Today's collectionsPayments posted today, split by method. Compare with the cash drawer and the bank slip before day close.

Reading the dashboard honestly

Tiles are computed from the operational database on request; they are not maintained counters. That means they are always consistent with the documents behind them, and it also means a tile can change while you are looking at it if a colleague records a delivery. There is no stale cache to reason about, and no nightly job that could leave a number wrong until morning.

Each tile is a link. A count without a route to the underlying records is a number nobody can act on, so every tile opens a filtered list — open passes, due-today passes, unbilled deliveries — with the filter already applied and visible in the toolbar.

◆45◆
4 · User Manual — Laundry AppLoveLaundry — System Manual

Daily rhythm

Table 21 — Typical use of the dashboard through the day
WhenLook atWhy
OpeningDue today, ready for deliveryPlan the routes and the wash order before the first van leaves.
MiddayOpen passes, linen discrepanciesCatch missing items while the shift that handled them is still on site.
Before dispatchReady for delivery, due todayConfirm that what is on the rack matches what the client expects.
EveningUnbilled deliveries, outstanding balanceRaise missing bills and chase balances before day close.
Day closeToday's collectionsReconcile cash and card totals against the drawer.
Warning

A dashboard that shows zero unbilled deliveries at the end of the day is only meaningful if every delivery was recorded as it happened. Recording a week of deliveries retrospectively makes the figures look correct while destroying their value for decisions.

4.3 Gate passes

The gate-pass register is the operational spine of the laundry. Every collection is recorded here, every delivery refers back to a pass, and every bill is built from delivered quantities. A pass records who sent what, when it arrived and when it is promised back.

Columns and statuses

The register shows the pass number, the client, the date received, the promised return date, the item count and the current status. Statuses advance only through recorded actions: received when the pass is created, in wash when the linen room starts processing, ready when finishing is complete, delivered when a delivery is recorded against it, and closed when nothing further is outstanding. A pass is never deleted; a mistake is corrected by cancelling the pass with a reason, which leaves it visible in the register.

4.4 Creating a gate pass

A gate pass is created at the moment goods are handed over. Doing it later, from memory, is the single largest source of billing disputes, because the quantities recorded then are guesses rather than counts.

◆46◆
4 · User Manual — Laundry AppLoveLaundry — System Manual

Procedure — creating a gate pass

  1. From the register, select + New gate pass.
  2. Choose the client. If the client is not listed, stop and ask an administrator to create the client record; do not type a variant of an existing name, which splits the client's history.
  3. Set the date received to the actual handover date. Back-dating a pass distorts the monthly matrix and the day-close totals for both dates.
  4. Set the promised return date. This is the date the client has been told; it drives the due-today worklist.
  5. Add each item line: item, service, quantity and rate. Count the goods as you add them — the pass is a receipt as well as a work order.
  6. Check the item count and estimated total against the physical count one more time. A typo here propagates into the delivery and the bill.
  7. Select Save & print gate pass and hand the printed copy to the client's driver. The pass is now locked for quantity edits except by a manager, and every such edit is audited.
Warning

Never create a pass for goods that have not arrived. A pass is evidence of possession; creating one early turns a missing delivery into a billing dispute.

4.5 Deliveries

A delivery records the return of finished goods against a gate pass. It is the bridge between operations and money: quantities delivered are what the client is billed for, and the delivery date determines the billing period.

Partial and split deliveries

Clients rarely receive a whole pass at once. A hotel may take back its sheets today and its towels tomorrow, and the platform expects this. Each delivery carries its own quantities per line, and the pass remains open until the delivered quantity equals the received quantity on every line, or until a supervisor closes the balance as short-delivered with a reason.

◆47◆
4 · User Manual — Laundry AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
Table 22 — Delivery rules
SituationWhat the system does
Delivered < receivedPass stays open; remaining quantity is shown as outstanding on the pass and in the due-today tile.
Delivered = receivedPass status becomes delivered; the lines become billable.
Delivered > receivedRejected. An over-delivery means either the pass quantity or the delivery count is wrong; correct the record rather than forcing the number.
Short delivery closedRequires a reason and a supervisor. The undelivered quantity is written off explicitly and appears in the discrepancy report.
Delivery corrected after billingRequires a credit note; the original delivery is not edited once a bill has consumed it.

Procedure — recording a delivery

  1. Open Deliveries and select Record delivery, or open the pass and choose Deliver from its detail view.
  2. Scan or select the gate pass. The form loads every line with the outstanding quantity prefilled.
  3. Reduce quantities to what is actually being handed over. Leave a line at zero if nothing on it is going out.
  4. Confirm the receiver's name — the person signing at the client — and the delivery date and time.
  5. Select Save delivery. The pass status recalculates immediately and the dashboard tiles update.
  6. Print or share the delivery note if the client requires one. The note shows quantities only, never rates.

What a delivery is not

  • Not a bill. Delivering goods does not raise an invoice. Bills are raised deliberately, in a batch or per client, so that the billing period is a business decision rather than a side effect of a van leaving.
  • Not a payment. A delivery can be made on credit. The balance appears on the bill, and payment is a separate record with its own audit trail.
  • Not reversible by deletion. A delivery recorded in error is reversed with a reason, which leaves both records visible. Deleting one would hide the fact that goods may have left the premises.
Note

The receiver's name matters more than it appears to. When a hotel later disputes a delivery, the name and timestamp on the note are the evidence that resolves it — which is why the field is required and is not defaulted to the signed-in user.

4.6 Bills

A bill is raised against a client for deliveries in a period. It states quantities, rates, charges, discounts and tax, and it carries the balance outstanding. Bills are the platform's commercial record: once issued, a bill is not edited, because an edited invoice cannot be reconciled against the copy the client holds.

Raising a bill

◆48◆
4 · User Manual — Laundry AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
  1. Open Bills and select Raise bill.
  2. Choose the client and the period. The form lists every unbilled delivery for that client in the period, with its pass reference.
  3. Select the deliveries to include. Deliveries already on another bill are not offered, which prevents double billing at the source.
  4. Review the line rates. Rates come from the client's agreed price list where one exists; a manual override requires bill:write and is visible on the bill as an edited rate.
  5. Apply any discount or adjustment with a reason. A discount without a reason is a control failure, not a courtesy.
  6. Check the totals: subtotal, discount, tax and amount due. Tax is computed from the configured rate, not typed.
  7. Select Issue bill. The bill receives its number, becomes immutable, and the client's balance increases.
  8. Print or share the bill. The print layout is produced by the guest-billing view, which shows the same figures as the screen.
Table 23 — Bill numbering and identity
AttributeRule
NumberAssigned on issue, sequential within the laundry and the financial year. Numbers are never reused, including for cancelled bills.
Statusdraft before issue, issued after, part-paid or paid as payments arrive, void if cancelled with a reason.
ImmutabilityIssued bills do not change. Corrections are credit notes or adjustment records that reference the original.
CurrencyOne currency per laundry, set in configuration; bills do not convert.

Draft, issue, and the point of no return

A draft bill can be edited freely — lines added, rates corrected, the period changed. Issuing it is the point at which it becomes a financial document: the number is consumed, the client can see it in the hotel portal if they have an account, and any correction must be made by a visible adjustment rather than an edit. Staff who are unsure whether a bill is right should leave it in draft; a draft is invisible to the client, and nothing is lost by waiting.

What goes on a bill

  • Only delivered quantities. Work in progress is not billable, however far advanced it is.
  • Rates that were agreed for that client, at the version in force on the delivery date.
  • Adjustments from returns or short deliveries, shown as separate lines rather than netted silently into quantities.
  • Tax computed by the platform from configuration, with the rate stated on the face of the bill.
Warning

If a bill total looks wrong after issue, do not edit the bill. Raise a credit note or an additional charge and reference the original. Editing an issued bill breaks the client's copy, the statement and the audit trail at once.

◆49◆
4 · User Manual — Laundry AppLoveLaundry — System Manual

4.7 · Bill detail and payments

Bill detail and payments

A bill's detail view is the client's account in miniature: what was billed, what has been paid, what remains, and every document that produced those figures. Payments recorded here are the only way a balance falls.

Table 24 — Payment methods and their effect
MethodRecorded asEffect on balance
CashReceipt against the bill, with drawer referenceReduces balance immediately
CardReceipt with terminal referenceReduces balance on posting; settlement is a banking matter
Bank transferReceipt with transfer referenceReduces balance when posted, not when the bank clears
ChequeReceipt with cheque number and bankReduces balance on posting; bounced cheques are reversed
Credit adjustmentAdjustment record with reasonReduces balance without cash; audited separately

Procedure — recording a payment

  1. Open the bill from Bills or from the client's account view.
  2. Select Record payment. The amount due is prefilled; overwrite it for a part payment.
  3. Choose the method and enter the reference — drawer slip, terminal slip or transfer reference. A payment without a reference cannot be reconciled at day close.
  4. Set the payment date to the date the money was received, not the date it was entered.
  5. Select Post payment. The balance recalculates and the bill status moves to part-paid or paid.
  6. Print the receipt if the client is present, and file the slip with the day's takings.

Reversals, not deletions

A payment posted in error is reversed, never deleted. The reversal creates a negative record that references the original, so the client's statement shows both the mistake and its correction. Deleting a payment would make the day-close total disagree with the bank without explanation — the classic symptom that turns a five-minute correction into an audit.

Warning

Applying a payment to the wrong bill is corrected by reversing it and re-posting to the correct bill. Never edit the original amount: the receipt the client holds would no longer match the record.

4.8 · Quotations

Quotations

A quotation is a priced offer. It carries line items, rates, validity and terms, and it can be converted into operational work — but it never becomes a bill by itself. The separation matters: a quotation is a promise about price, while a bill is a statement of work actually delivered.

◆50◆
4 · User Manual — Laundry AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
Table 25 — Quotation states
StateMeaningAllowed next steps
draftBeing prepared; not visible to the clientEdit, send, discard
sentIssued to the client with a validity dateAccept, decline, expire, revise
acceptedClient has agreed the priceConvert to gate pass or client rate card
declinedClient rejected the offerRevise as a new draft
expiredValidity date passed without a decisionRe-issue with a new validity date

Procedure — preparing a quotation

  1. Select Quotations → New quotation and choose the prospective or existing client.
  2. Add line items: item, service, quantity and rate. Use the item catalogue where possible so that the wording matches the eventual bill.
  3. Set the validity period. A quotation without an end date is a price the laundry may be held to indefinitely.
  4. Review the totals and any terms, then select Send or Mark as sent once the client has received it.
  5. When the client accepts, record the acceptance and convert the quotation. Conversion creates a draft gate pass or updates the client's rate card; it does not create a bill.

AI assistance

The quotation module can draft line items and wording through the AI chat surface. Drafts are suggestions: every rate and quantity must be reviewed before the quotation is sent, and the platform records who issued it, not what suggested it. The assistant has no ability to send a quotation or to change a price without a user action.

Note

A converted quotation is linked to its source. When a client later disputes a rate, the chain from quotation to pass to bill is visible in one place.

4.9 · Workers

Workers

The worker register records the people who do the work and, where the laundry pays by output, the work attributed to them. It is deliberately simple: identity, role, status and assignment. Payroll arithmetic belongs to the accounting service, not to the operational record.

Table 26 — Worker record
FieldPurposeNotes
Worker codeShort identifier used on production sheetsUnique within the laundry
NameDisplay name on assignment listsEditable; historical records keep the name at the time
RoleWasher, presser, driver, checker, supervisorDrives which worklists the worker appears in
StatusActive, on leave, inactiveInactive workers cannot be assigned new work
ContactPhone for shift coordinationOptional; treated as personal data
◆51◆
4 · User Manual — Laundry AppLoveLaundry — System Manual

Procedure — adding a worker

  1. Open Workers and select Add worker.
  2. Enter the worker code exactly as it appears on the laundry's own records; the code is how production sheets are reconciled.
  3. Set the role and status. A worker who has left is set to inactive rather than deleted, because historic assignments reference them.
  4. Save. The worker appears in assignment lists for the roles selected.

Assignment and accountability

Work can be attributed to a worker at the gate-pass level, the item-line level, or at the wash batch level in the linen room. Attribution is optional for operations and essential for piece-rate payroll: if a laundry pays by item, the assignment is the evidence of who processed what. Where attribution is used, it must be recorded at the time of work, not reconstructed at the end of the week.

Note

Attendance and salary records live in laundry-management, not here. The worker register supplies identity to both, so a name change in one place does not silently diverge from the other.

4.10 · Reports and the monthly matrix

Reports and the monthly matrix

Reports answer questions that outlive the day. They are computed from the same operational documents as the dashboards, so a report never disagrees with the screen it summarises — and a report is only as good as the discipline with which passes and deliveries were recorded.

Table 27 — Available reports
ReportAnswersTypical use
Daily productionWhat was received, washed and delivered on a dateShift handover and capacity planning
Client statementEvery bill, payment and balance for one clientMonth-end credit control
Monthly matrixQuantities and values by client by dayContract reconciliation and volume checks
Unbilled deliveriesDelivered work not yet on a billRevenue at risk before day close
Linen discrepancyMissing, damaged and short-delivered itemsLoss investigation and client conversations
Worker productivityItems or batches attributed per workerPiece-rate payroll and scheduling

The monthly matrix

The matrix is a grid: clients down the side, days of the month across the top, and a cell for each day holding the quantity and value processed for that client. It exists because a monthly total hides the pattern that matters — a client whose volume collapses for four days, or a day on which one client's items were entered against another's name.

◆52◆
4 · User Manual — Laundry AppLoveLaundry — System Manual

Rows are clients, columns are calendar days, and the final columns total the month. Cells are derived from gate passes (received) and deliveries (returned), so the matrix is a view, not a ledger: nothing is typed into it, and it cannot be edited. A cell that looks wrong is a pass that was entered wrongly, and that is where the correction belongs.

Note

Export the matrix before a contract review. It is the document clients recognise, and it is generated from the same records that produced their bills.

4.11 · Day close

Day close

Day close is the point at which a business date stops moving. It freezes the day's totals, confirms that every delivery has been billed or consciously deferred, and records who closed the day and when. It is a control, not a formality: most reconciliation failures are discovered at close, which is exactly when they are cheapest to fix.

Procedure — closing the day

  1. Confirm that all gate passes for the date are recorded. Compare the register with the paper collection book.
  2. Confirm that all deliveries made today are recorded and that no pass is left open without a reason.
  3. Check Unbilled deliveries. Raise the missing bills, or record why a delivery is intentionally held into the next period.
  4. Reconcile Today's collections against the cash drawer and the card terminal report. Record any difference with an explanation.
  5. Review linen discrepancies raised during the day and confirm that each has an owner.
  6. Select Close day. The system writes a day-close record with totals, the operator and a timestamp.
  7. Print or save the close summary and attach it to the day's banking.
Table 28 — What the close freezes
ItemEffect of closing
Bill totalsFigures for the date become the reported figures; later corrections appear on the date they are made
Payment totalsCollections for the date are fixed for reconciliation
Delivery countsVolumes reported in the monthly matrix stop changing for that day
Day-close recordImmutable; a correction requires a reopening with a reason
Warning

Do not close a day to make a warning disappear. A closed day with an unresolved discrepancy is harder to correct than an open one, because reopening is itself an audited event.

◆53◆
4 · User Manual — Laundry AppLoveLaundry — System Manual

4.12 · Administration, users and common errors

Administration, users and common errors

Administration in the laundry app is limited to the tenant you are signed in to: users, their memberships and roles, and hotel client accounts for your own clients. Creating a laundry is a platform operation, described in Chapter 8.1, and is not available from this application.

Users and roles

A user is a person with a login. A membership is that person's link to your laundry, carrying their role. Removing someone's access means removing the membership, not deleting the user — they may belong to another laundry, and their history on your records must remain attributable.

Table 29 — Common errors and what to do
Message or symptomUsual causeAction
403 — tenant could not be resolvedToken issued without a tenant, or a client token used on a staff routeSign out and sign in again; hotel accounts must use the Hotel Desk app
403 — capability requiredRole lacks the capability for this actionAsk an administrator to review the membership role
409 — duplicate pass numberTwo passes created from the same paper docketOpen both, keep the correct one, cancel the other with a reason
422 — quantity exceeds receivedDelivery quantity larger than the pass lineRecount; correct the pass quantity with a manager if the pass was wrong
Bill total differs from the printBill edited after issue, or printed from a stale tabReload the bill; issued bills cannot change, so a difference indicates a stale view
Dashboard tile shows zeroFilter applied, or the day is closedClear the date filter; check the day-close record
Note

Errors that mention a capability or a tenant are authorisation outcomes, not faults. Report the exact message to an administrator; it names what was missing.

4.13 · Day-close sequence

Day-close sequence

What has to be true before a date can be frozen, and what happens when it is not.

◆54◆
4 · User Manual — Laundry AppLoveLaundry — System Manual

Closing a day is a transaction with a precondition, not a button that writes a total. The service counts unbilled deliveries first; if any exist, it refuses and returns the list. Nothing is frozen, so the operator can correct the cause and try again.

When the close succeeds, the totals and the close record commit together. That single unit is what makes the day's figures defensible: there is no state in which a date is marked closed but its totals were never written.

Rule

A close that fails is cheaper than a close that succeeds with an unresolved discrepancy. Reopening is itself an audited event and is never the first resort.

Part Two · User Manual — Shop Counter App

User Manual — Shop Counter App

◆

A point-of-sale surface for walk-in customers: fast, narrow, and reconciled at the end of every shift.

5.1 Overview and sign-in

The Shop Counter app is the shop-app front end. It serves a different transaction from the laundry: a customer arrives with a bag, not an account, and leaves with a receipt. Everything about the interface follows from that: few required fields, large targets, keyboard-first entry, and a day close that reconciles takings rather than work in progress.

Table 30 — Shop Counter at a glance
AttributeValue
Applicationshop-app — React 19, TypeScript, Vite 8, Tailwind 4
Development port5174

Session keyll_shop_session
