5 · User Manual — Shop Counter AppLoveLaundry — System Manual

Procedure — signing in at the counter

  1. Open the Shop Counter app on the counter terminal.
  2. Enter your own staff email and password, then select Sign in.
  3. Confirm the laundry name in the header is your shop, and that the date shown is today.
  4. Leave the session open for the shift. The token lasts 24 hours, but a shared terminal should be signed out at handover.
Warning

Never sign in with a colleague's account to “save time”. Every void, refund and discount is attributed to the signed-in user, and a shared login makes those actions unattributable.

5.2 · Today view

Today view

The today view is the shop's home screen and, for most staff, the only screen they need between customers. It answers three questions: what have I taken today, what is waiting to be finished, and what did the last few transactions look like?

What the tiles mean

Takings today is the sum of paid shop bills for the business date, split by tender in the detail. Open bills are transactions started but not settled — held garments awaiting collection, or a bill left open while the customer finds a card. Refunds counts refunds recorded today and flags that each requires supervisor approval. The shift panel names who opened the till and when day close becomes available.

Warning

A large open-bill count at closing time usually means bills were abandoned mid-transaction rather than held deliberately. Resolve them before day close; an abandoned bill is a customer who left without paying and without a receipt.

◆57◆
5 · User Manual — Shop Counter AppLoveLaundry — System Manual

5.3 · Bills

Shop bills

Shop bills are counter sales. They carry their own numbering, separate from laundry bills, because they are a different kind of document: a completed retail transaction rather than a periodic charge for work done. Keeping them separate means shop takings reconcile cleanly and laundry receivables are not diluted by walk-in cash.

Table 31 — Shop bill states
StateMeaningWhat is still possible
draftItems added, not yet taken to paymentEdit lines, apply discount, abandon
openPayment not completed; customer may returnComplete payment, hold, add items
paidTendered and receiptedReprint, refund with approval
refundedFully reversed after paymentNone; a new bill is required for new goods
voidCancelled before payment, with a reasonNone; the number is retained

Procedure — completing a sale

  1. Select Quick bill, or open an existing draft bill.
  2. Add items: choose from the catalogue or type a free line where the catalogue has no entry.
  3. Confirm quantities and rates aloud with the customer before taking payment.
  4. Select the tender: cash or card. For cash, enter the amount tendered so the change is calculated and shown.
  5. Select Take payment. The bill moves to paid and the receipt is offered for printing.
  6. Hand over the receipt and the goods together. The receipt is the customer's evidence of the transaction and the shop's evidence of the tender.

Discounts and their limits

A discount is a line-level or bill-level reduction with a reason. Counter staff may apply the configured standard discount; anything beyond it requires a supervisor, and the reason is recorded against the bill. The point is not to prevent generosity but to make it visible: a discount without a reason is indistinguishable from an error, and at month end it is indistinguishable from theft.

Note

Voided and refunded bills keep their numbers. Reconciling a day's takings against a bill sequence with gaps is far harder than reconciling one where every number is accounted for.

5.4 · Quick bill

Quick bill

Quick bill is the counter's fast path: a numeric keypad, the most-used services as one-touch buttons, and a single total. It exists because the difference between a twelve-second and a forty-second transaction is the difference between a queue and a complaint.

◆58◆
5 · User Manual — Shop Counter AppLoveLaundry — System Manual

Procedure — a cash sale in under a minute

  1. Select Quick bill from the header.
  2. Tap the service buttons for each garment type; adjust quantity with the keypad if more than one.
  3. Read the total to the customer and confirm the item count.
  4. Select Cash, enter the amount tendered, and confirm the change shown.
  5. Print the receipt. The bill is now paid and appears in today's takings.

Card sales follow the same path with the Card tender; the terminal is separate, and the app records the reference so the day close can be reconciled against the terminal report. Split tender is used when a customer pays part cash and part card, and the app requires both amounts to sum to the total before it will accept the payment.

Note

Quick bill never creates a laundry bill, a gate pass or a linen record. If a customer wants laundry service rather than a counter sale, use the laundry app.

5.5 · Day close

Day close at the counter

The shop's day close is shorter than the laundry's, and it has one job: prove that the money in the drawer matches the money recorded. Everything else — bills raised, refunds given, discounts applied — is detail that explains a difference, not a difference itself.

Procedure — closing the shop day

◆59◆
5 · User Manual — Shop Counter AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
  1. Resolve every open bill: complete payment, or void it with a reason.
  2. Count the drawer and record the counted amount in the close form.
  3. Compare the counted amount with the system's cash total. If they differ, enter the difference and a short explanation before closing.
  4. Check that card takings match the terminal's end-of-day report.
  5. Review refunds and discounts recorded during the shift; each must have an approver.
  6. Select Close day. The close record is written with totals, the operator and a timestamp.
  7. Print the close summary, attach the terminal report and the bank slip, and hand both to the supervisor.
Table 32 — Reconciliation items
ItemSource of truthTolerance
Cash takingsPhysical drawer countAny difference is recorded, not adjusted away
Card takingsTerminal end-of-day reportMust match to the cent; a mismatch is investigated before close
RefundsRefund records with approverEach must be approved; unapproved refunds block close
Open billsBill list filtered to openMust be zero, or explicitly held with a reason
Warning

Closing the day does not move money. If the drawer is short, record the shortage and escalate; do not take cash from a later sale to balance the day.

5.6 · Roles and permissions

Roles and permissions at the counter

The shop uses the same staff roles as the rest of the platform, with capabilities scoped to counter work. A shop user is a member of the laundry with a role; there is no separate shop-only account type. That keeps one identity per person across the business and one audit trail.

Table 33 — Shop roles
RoleCan doCannot do
STAFFCreate quick bills, complete payment, reprint receipts, hold billsGive refunds, exceed standard discount, close day, void a paid bill
MANAGERAll counter actions, refunds, discounts beyond standard, day close, reprint any billChange user roles, alter shop configuration
ADMINEverything a manager can, plus user and membership management for the laundryCreate laundries or act outside the tenant

How the controls appear

The app hides actions the signed-in user cannot perform, so a counter assistant does not see a refund button they are not allowed to use. That is a courtesy, not the control: every action is re-checked on the server against the capability carried in the token. If a hidden action is somehow invoked — a stale tab, a crafted request — it fails with a permission error and an audit entry.

◆60◆
5 · User Manual — Shop Counter AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
Table 34 — Capability mapping
ActionCapabilityHeld by
Create or pay a shop billbill:writeSTAFF, MANAGER, ADMIN
View bills and takingsbill:readSTAFF, MANAGER, ADMIN
Post or reverse a paymentpayment:writeMANAGER, ADMIN
View the day-close reportreport:readMANAGER, ADMIN
Open the dashboarddashboard:readSTAFF, MANAGER, ADMIN
Note

A refund is a payment reversal in accounting terms, which is why it needs payment:write and therefore a manager. This is a deliberate restriction, not an oversight.

5.7 · Procedures

Counter procedures

The four procedures below cover almost every exception a counter encounters. Each is written to be followed under time pressure, with a customer waiting.

Procedure — refunding a paid bill

  1. Open the bill from Today or search its number.
  2. Select Refund. The full amount is prefilled; reduce it for a partial refund.
  3. Enter the reason and select the refund tender: cash, or reversal to the original card.
  4. Call a supervisor to approve. The approval is recorded against the refund with the approver's name.
  5. Hand over the cash or confirm the card reversal, and print the refund slip.

Procedure — voiding a bill before payment

  1. Open the open bill and select Void.
  2. Enter the reason: wrong item, customer left, duplicate entry.
  3. Confirm. The bill keeps its number and disappears from the open list.

Procedure — holding a bill

Use Hold bill when a customer steps away or goes to fetch a card. A held bill stays in the open list with its items intact; it is not a credit sale and it does not reserve stock. At shift handover, resolve every held bill — complete it, void it, or write down why it remains open.

Procedure — reprinting a receipt

Open the paid bill and select Reprint. The reprint carries the same number and a duplicate marker so that two copies cannot be presented as two transactions. Reprints are audited; a pattern of reprints on the same bill is worth a supervisor's attention.

◆61◆
5 · User Manual — Shop Counter AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
Warning

Never re-enter a sale to correct a receipt. That creates a second bill and inflates takings; void the original and re-enter once, or reprint it.

5.8 · Shift handover and reconciliation

Shift handover and reconciliation

Most counter discrepancies are born at handover: a bill left open by one shift, a drawer counted by nobody, a refund approved verbally. A short, disciplined handover is cheaper than any reconciliation at month end.

Table 35 — Handover checklist
CheckDone whenEvidence
Open bills resolvedNo bill left open without a written reasonOpen-bill list printed or photographed
Drawer countedCount agreed by both shiftsCount slip signed by both
Card report matchedTerminal total equals recorded card takingsTerminal report attached
Refunds accountedEach refund has an approver recordedRefund list with approver column
Petty cashAny shop float returned to the agreed amountFloat note
Session closedSigned-out terminal, or explicit handover of the sessionSign-out recorded in the log

When the drawer does not match

  1. Recount before concluding anything. Most differences are a miscount of notes of one denomination.
  2. Check the card terminal report against recorded card takings; a card entry keyed as cash is the most common single cause.
  3. Review the shift's bills for a total that was edited after payment, or a bill voided after cash was taken.
  4. Record the remaining difference with an explanation in the day-close form. Do not adjust a bill to absorb it.
  5. Escalate a difference above the shop's agreed threshold to the supervisor the same day.
Note

Differences are recorded, never absorbed. An absorbed difference hides a pattern, and a pattern is the only way to find a genuine problem.

5.9 · Common errors

Shop Counter — common errors

The messages below account for nearly all counter incidents. Each names what the system refused and why; the action column is written for the person at the till, not for an engineer.

◆62◆
5 · User Manual — Shop Counter AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
Table 36 — Common errors at the counter
MessageCauseAction
401 — session expiredToken older than 24 hours, or the terminal's clock movedSign in again; if it recurs, check the terminal clock
403 — payment:write requiredA refund or reversal attempted by STAFFCall a supervisor to approve with their own account
422 — tender does not equal totalSplit payment entered with a missing amountRe-enter both amounts; the app requires them to sum exactly
409 — bill already paidTwo terminals completed the same billOpen the bill, confirm the tender, refund the duplicate
Bill not foundFiltered to today, bill belongs to an earlier dateClear the date filter and search by number
Printer shows nothingPrint dialog sent to a paused queueCheck the printer queue; the bill is already saved and can be reprinted
Day close blockedOpen bills or unapproved refunds remainResolve the listed items, then close again

When to stop and call for help

Stop and escalate if the app shows a total that disagrees with the items, if a paid bill cannot be found, or if the drawer difference exceeds the shop's threshold. In each case the correct action is to preserve the state — do not void, refund or re-enter — and to record what was on screen, because a second transaction taken to “fix” the first is what turns a reportable discrepancy into an unexplainable one.

Note

Report the exact message text. “It wouldn't let me” cannot be diagnosed; “403 payment:write required” identifies the cause immediately.

User Manual — Hotel Desk App

◆

A read-only portal in which a hotel sees its own laundry records — and nothing else.

6.1 Hotel client sign-in

The Hotel Desk app is the hotel-app front end. It is used by hotel front-office and housekeeping managers to check what they sent, what came back, and what they owe. It is not a staff application and it cannot change operational records: a hotel observes, it does not edit.

Table 37 — Hotel Desk at a glance

Procedure — signing in as a hotel

6 · User Manual — Hotel Desk AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
  1. Open the Hotel Desk app. Use the hotel's client account, not a staff account — staff credentials are refused by the client sign-in endpoint.
  2. Enter the client account email and password and select Sign in.
  3. Confirm the property name shown in the header matches your hotel. If it does not, stop: you are looking at another property's account and must report it immediately.
  4. Leave the session to expire, or sign out at the end of the shift. Sessions last 12 hours.
Warning

A hotel session carries no tenant claim and no staff role. It cannot be used in the laundry, shop or linen-room applications; those applications will reject it. This is by design, not a fault to work around.

Note

If the account is locked or the password is lost, contact the laundry that issued the account. The hotel cannot reset its own credentials from this application.

6.2 · Overview

Overview

The overview is the hotel's single screen: what is currently with the laundry, what has been returned this month, what is outstanding financially. Every figure is filtered by the hotel's own client_name within the issuing laundry, so no other property's volume can appear in a total.

Reading the tiles

The four tiles are deliberately operational rather than analytical. With the laundry counts open gate passes and the items on them; returned this month counts delivered items in the current calendar month; outstanding is the unpaid balance across issued invoices; and the statement period links to the current statement. None of these figures includes another client's data, and none can be re-scoped by the hotel.

◆65◆
6 · User Manual — Hotel Desk AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
Note

A hotel cannot change the date range of a total on the overview. Period selection belongs to the statement, where the boundaries are explicit and the document is designed to be printed.

6.3 · Gate passes

Gate passes (hotel view)

The hotel's gate-pass list shows every pass raised for its property: the date the goods were collected, the promised return date, the item count and the current status. It is the operational answer to “where is our linen?”

Table 38 — Columns in the hotel gate-pass list
ColumnMeaning
Pass numberThe laundry's reference; quote it in any query
ReceivedDate the laundry took possession of the goods
Due backPromised return date
ItemsTotal quantity on the pass
StatusReceived, in wash, ready, delivered, closed
Last updateWhen the status last changed

What the hotel can see on a pass

The hotel sees the items, the quantities, the service type and the status history. It does not see rates on the pass view — pricing is a commercial matter between the laundry and the property, stated on the invoice — and it never sees the laundry's internal cost, worker assignment or route information.

Procedure — finding a pass

  1. Open Gate passes.
  2. Filter by date range if you know when the goods were collected, or search by pass number from the laundry's collection note.
  3. Open the pass to see its item lines and status history.
  4. If the status has not moved when you expect it to, contact the laundry quoting the pass number rather than raising a new pass; there is no way to create a pass from this application.
Warning

A hotel cannot create, edit or cancel a gate pass. A missing pass is a laundry-side data entry issue: report it with the collection date and the driver's name, and the laundry will raise or correct it.

6.4 · Deliveries

Deliveries (hotel view)

Deliveries show what has come back, when, and in what quantity. For a hotel, this is the operational record that supports housekeeping's own counts — and the evidence used when an invoice quantity is questioned.

◆66◆
6 · User Manual — Hotel Desk AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
Table 39 — Delivery information visible to a hotel
FieldWhy it matters
Delivery date and timeMatches the property's receiving log
Pass referenceLinks the delivery to what was sent
Items and quantitiesWhat was actually returned, line by line
Received byThe name recorded by the laundry at handover
Partial indicatorShows that a pass is only partly returned

Partial deliveries

A pass may come back in several deliveries. The hotel sees each one separately, with the outstanding quantity on the pass. This is normal for large properties where sheets and towels are processed in different batches, and it is not a discrepancy.

Procedure — reconciling a delivery

  1. Open Deliveries and filter to the date of receipt.
  2. Compare the quantities on each delivery with the property's receiving sheet, line by line.
  3. Where a line differs, note the pass number, the item and both quantities before contacting the laundry.
  4. Report the difference the same day. A difference found a week later cannot be checked against the laundry floor.
  5. Do not sign for a delivery you have not counted; the recorded receiver is the evidence that the count was accepted.
Note

Deliveries are read-only here. If a count was signed for in error, the correction is made by the laundry and appears in the history, including the reason.

6.5 · Invoices

Invoices

An invoice is the hotel's bill: quantities delivered in a period, at the agreed rates, with tax and the balance outstanding. The hotel can open an invoice, read its lines and download it — but it cannot alter it, and it cannot raise one.

Table 40 — Invoice states visible to the hotel
StateWhat it means for the property
IssuedPayable; the amount due is shown on the invoice
Part paidSome payment has been recorded; the remainder is shown
PaidSettled in full; no action required
VoidCancelled by the laundry; a replacement may exist — check the statement
◆67◆
6 · User Manual — Hotel Desk AppLoveLaundry — System Manual

Procedure — checking an invoice

  1. Open Invoices and select the period or invoice number.
  2. Open the invoice and compare its lines with your own receiving records for the same period.
  3. Download the PDF if you need it for internal approval. The download is the same document the laundry holds.
  4. Where a line is disputed, quote the invoice number, the line and the pass reference in your query to the laundry.
  5. Do not withhold payment for one disputed line without telling the laundry: a short payment without explanation appears as an aged balance and may suspend service.

What an invoice does not show

Invoices state quantities and agreed rates. They do not show the laundry's internal costs, worker productivity, other clients' rates, or the composition of any discount beyond the line description. Those are outside the client relationship and are not exposed by any hotel endpoint.

Warning

If an invoice includes a pass you do not recognise, do not pay it and do not ignore it. Report it with the pass number the same day; a misposted pass is easy to correct before the period closes and hard afterwards.

6.6 · Statements

Statements

A statement lists every invoice, payment and adjustment for a period with a running balance. It is the document a hotel's finance team reconciles against its own ledger, and it is the reason the portal exists for many properties.

Table 41 — Statement contents
SectionContent
Opening balanceAmount outstanding at the start of the period
InvoicesEach invoice with date, number and amount
PaymentsEach payment received, with method and reference
AdjustmentsCredit notes and corrections, each with a reason
Closing balanceOpening balance plus invoices, less payments and credits

Procedure — reconciling a statement

◆68◆
6 · User Manual — Hotel Desk AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
  1. Open Statements and select the period. The default is the current month to date.
  2. Print or download the statement for your finance file.
  3. Match each invoice to your approved purchase record.
  4. Match each payment to your bank or petty-cash record. A payment recorded by the laundry but not yet cleared in your bank will appear here before it appears there — that is timing, not error.
  5. Query any unmatched line with its reference. The closing balance is the figure that must agree, not the individual lines alone.
Note

Statements are generated on request from the laundry's records. A statement downloaded twice in a day may differ if a payment was posted in between, so always keep the version you reconciled against.

6.7 · What a hotel can and cannot do

What a hotel can and cannot do

The hotel portal is read-only by design. The table below is the complete statement of a hotel account's authority; anything not listed as permitted is refused by the server, not merely hidden in the interface.

Table 42 — Hotel permissions
ActionPermittedNotes
View own gate passesYesFiltered by laundry_id and client_name
View own deliveriesYesIncludes partial deliveries
View and download own invoicesYesIssued documents only; drafts are invisible
View and download own statementsYesAny period within retention
Create or edit a gate passNoLaundry staff only
Record or amend a deliveryNoLaundry staff only
Raise, edit or void an invoiceNoIssued invoices are immutable for everyone
Post a paymentNoPayments are recorded by the laundry
View another property's recordsNoDifferent client_name; no endpoint accepts a name parameter
View rates, costs or worker dataNoOutside the client relationship
Manage hotel user accountsNoHOTEL_ADMIN manages its own users only through the laundry

Why read-only

A hotel that could edit its own records could dispute an invoice by changing the evidence. Making the portal read-only removes that possibility entirely and makes the portal's data credible to both parties: what the hotel sees is exactly what the laundry recorded, unmediated.

Note

HOTEL_ADMIN and HOTEL_MANAGER differ in what they can see of the account's commercial detail, not in what they can change. Neither role can change operational data.

6.8 · Procedures

Hotel desk procedures

These are the five tasks a hotel performs in the portal. All of them end in reading or downloading; none of them changes a laundry record.

Procedure — checking what is still with the laundry

  1. Open Overview and read the with the laundry tile.
  2. Open Gate passes and filter to open statuses.
  3. For each pass, check the due-back date against housekeeping's requirement for the coming days.
  4. If a pass is overdue, contact the laundry with the pass number and the date it was due.

Procedure — preparing a month-end reconciliation

  1. Open Statements and select the closed month.
  2. Download the statement and every invoice referenced on it.
  3. Match invoices to approved purchase records and payments to bank entries.
  4. Record any unmatched item with its reference and raise a single consolidated query with the laundry.

Procedure — reporting a discrepancy

Collect the pass number or invoice number, the item description, the quantity you counted and the date. Send them in one message to the laundry's client contact. A query with references is resolved in minutes; a query without them requires the laundry to reconstruct the day.

Warning

Do not open a second account to check another property, and do not share credentials between properties. Each client account is scoped to one property; sharing it is a breach of the terms of use and destroys the audit trail.

6.9 · Common errors and support

Hotel desk — common errors and support

Support path

The hotel's first contact is the laundry that issued the account: they own the records, the invoicing and the client account itself. The laundry escalates to the platform operator only for authentication faults that survive a password reset — for example, a client account whose scope is missing or a token that is refused by every endpoint.

What to include in a support request

  • The property name and the client account email (never the password).
  • The exact message text and the time it occurred.
  • The pass or invoice number involved.
  • What you expected to see and what you saw instead.
Note

Hotel accounts are created and disabled by laundry administrators in the user-service client account screen. A hotel cannot create its own account, and there is no self-service registration.

6.10 · Hotel portal request path

Hotel portal request path

How one property's records are separated from every other property's, on every request.

◆71◆
6 · User Manual — Hotel Desk AppLoveLaundry — System Manual

The portal has no endpoint that accepts a client name as a parameter. The name comes from the token's scope, so a hotel cannot ask for another property's records even by guessing an identifier.

The dual filter is the mechanism: every query carries both the laundry and the client name. Filtering on the name alone would be unsafe across laundries; filtering on the laundry alone would expose every hotel to every other hotel.

Rule

A request for another property's invoice returns not-found, identical to an invoice that does not exist. The portal never confirms that another property's records exist.

Part Two · User Manual — Linen Room App

User Manual — Linen Room App

◆

Scan-driven tracking of every tagged item, from collection to retirement.

7.1 Overview and scanning

The Linen Room app is the linen-room-app front end, used on a tablet or handheld at the wash station. Its users work one-handed with a scanner, so the interface is a single scan field, a large current-item card, and a short list of valid next actions. Everything else is history.

Table 44 — Linen Room at a glance
AttributeValue
Applicationlinen-room-app — React 19, TypeScript, Vite 8, Tailwind 4
Development port5176
Sign-inStaff sign-in against user-service
Session keyll_linen_session
RolesLINEN_SUPERVISOR, HOUSEKEEPER
Capabilitieslinen:read, linen:scan, linen:write

Why scanning, not typing

7 · User Manual — Linen Room AppLoveLaundry — System Manual

A typed tag number is a guess with a keyboard. A scan is the identifier itself. The platform therefore treats the scan as the only way a lifecycle status advances: there is no “set status” dropdown, and no bulk action that moves items without reading them. If an item was not scanned, the record says it was not scanned — which is the truth the laundry needs when a client disputes a count.

Procedure — starting a shift at the station

  1. Sign in on the station device with your own linen-room account.
  2. Confirm the station name and the current batch or pass shown at the top.
  3. Test the scanner by scanning any tag already in hand; the item card should populate within a moment.
  4. Keep the scan field focused. If a scan produces no response, tap the field before scanning again rather than retyping the tag.
Warning

Do not share a station login between staff. Every scan is attributed to the signed-in user, and an unattributable scan is worthless when a discrepancy is investigated.

7.2 · Lifecycle statuses

Lifecycle statuses

Each tag moves through a fixed sequence. Statuses advance only by recording the action that caused the move, and each action is attributed to a user and a time. The sequence is enforced server-side: a scan that would skip a stage is rejected.

◆74◆
7 · User Manual — Linen Room AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
Table 45 — Actions and their meaning
ActionFrom → toWhen it is used
collectnew → collectedGoods picked up from the client or from the property's linen room
receivecollected → receivedCounted in at the laundry; discrepancies are raised here
start_washreceived → in washLoaded into a wash batch
complete_washin wash → washedBatch finished; items awaiting finishing
presswashed → pressedIroned or folded and inspected
readypressed → readyRacked and available for delivery
deliverready → deliveredHanded to the client against a delivery
mark_missingany active → missingItem cannot be found; requires a supervisor
mark_damagedany active → damagedItem is damaged; requires a supervisor
retireany → retiredItem withdrawn from service permanently
Note

There is no reverse transition. An item scanned into the wrong batch is corrected by recording the exception and re-scanning it into the correct batch, which leaves both events visible.

7.3 · Scan workflow

Scan workflow

The station screen is built around one loop: scan, confirm, act. The current item card shows what the platform knows, and the action buttons show only what is legal next — which is how a fast operator avoids invalid transitions without memorising the rules.

Procedure — scanning a batch through

◆75◆
7 · User Manual — Linen Room AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
  1. Scan the tag. The current tag card confirms the item and its current status.
  2. Check the item against the card — type, client and pass. A scan of the wrong item is worse than no scan.
  3. Select the next action. Only legal transitions are offered. The list updates immediately.
  4. Repeat for each item. The batch counter increments as items advance.
  5. When the batch is complete, confirm the batch total on screen against the physical count before moving the load.
Note

Scanning is idempotent: scanning the same tag twice for the same action does not duplicate the event. It is safer to scan again than to assume a scan registered.

7.4 · Inventory

Inventory

Inventory is the count of tags by status, item type and client. It is derived from scan history, so it is a live picture rather than a periodic stock take — and it is only as accurate as the scanning discipline behind it.

Table 46 — Inventory views
ViewShowsUse
By statusTags in each lifecycle stateSee what is in wash, ready or missing at a glance
By item typeSheets, duvet covers, towels, mats and so onCapacity planning and reorder decisions
By clientTags attributable to each client_nameClient-level reconciliation and loss conversations
By ageTags whose current status is older than expectedFind items stuck in a stage
RetiredTags withdrawn from serviceAsset history and replacement rate

What inventory is not

It is not a valuation. The platform counts tags and items, not their book value; asset accounting belongs to the accounting service and to the laundry's own fixed-asset register. It is also not a guarantee of physical presence: a tag can be scanned and then lost, which is exactly what the discrepancy process exists to catch.

Procedure — daily inventory check

  1. Open Inventory and select By status.
  2. Compare the in wash count with the batches physically on the floor. A large difference means items were loaded without scanning.
  3. Compare ready with the rack. Ready items that are not on the rack are either delivered without a scan or missing.
  4. Check By age for items in one status for longer than the wash cycle allows.
  5. Record any unexplained difference through the discrepancy process rather than adjusting the count.
◆76◆
7 · User Manual — Linen Room AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
Warning

Never correct inventory by retiring items to make the numbers match. Retirement is permanent and removes the asset from service; a missing item may still be found.

7.5 · Discrepancies

Discrepancies

A discrepancy is a recorded mismatch: an item counted in short, found damaged, or unaccounted for at the end of a batch. The platform records discrepancies rather than smoothing them away, because a pattern of loss is only visible if each instance survives.

Table 47 — Discrepancy types
TypeRaised whenEffect
Short receiptFewer items received than the pass statesPass line quantity is queried; client is notified
MissingItem cannot be found after a searchTag leaves the active batch; supervisor review
DamagedItem is torn, stained beyond recovery or otherwise unusableTag marked damaged; client liability assessed
Short deliveryFewer items delivered than the client expectedPass remains open or is closed short with a reason
UnscannedItem found physically but absent from the batch recordItem is scanned into the correct stage; cause noted

Procedure — recording a missing item

  1. Search the station, the batch and the rack before recording anything. Most missing items are in the previous batch.
  2. Scan or enter the tag and select mark_missing.
  3. Enter where it was last seen and what search was carried out.
  4. Confirm. The item leaves the active batch and appears in open discrepancies.
  5. Notify the supervisor, who decides whether to inform the client and whether to replace the item.

Closing a discrepancy

A discrepancy is closed when the item is found, when the client accepts the loss, or when it is written off with a reason. Closing is a supervisor action with an audit entry. An item found later is scanned back into the correct stage, which closes the missing record automatically and leaves both events in the tag's history.

Note

Discrepancy counts are part of the dashboard for a reason: a laundry that never records a discrepancy is usually not counting, not not losing.

7.6 · Tag printing

Tag printing

Tags are the physical identity of an item. Printing is therefore a controlled action: each printed tag is recorded, and a tag that is printed but never attached is a future discrepancy.

◆77◆
7 · User Manual — Linen Room AppLoveLaundry — System Manual
Table 48 — Tag printing rules
RuleReason
Tags are printed in batches linked to an item typeKeeps numbering readable and simplifies replacement
A printed tag is recorded as issuedAllows an unattached tag to be traced
Duplicate tags are never printed for an active itemTwo tags on one item double-counts inventory
A replacement tag is issued only after the old tag is retiredPrevents two live identities for one item
Printing requires linen:writeHOUSEKEEPER can scan but not print

Procedure — printing a tag batch

  1. Open Tags → Print batch.
  2. Choose the item type and the number of tags required.
  3. Select the printer and confirm that labels are loaded — a half-printed batch wastes tag numbers.
  4. Print, then apply each tag to an item immediately. Do not leave printed tags loose at the station.
  5. Confirm the batch in the app so that the tags are recorded as issued and attached.

Replacing a damaged tag

Where a tag is unreadable but the item is identifiable, retire the old tag and issue a replacement, recording the reason. Where the item is not identifiable, treat it as an unscanned item: count it, assign it to the client whose linen it matches, and record how the identification was made. Guessing the client is worse than leaving the item unassigned.

Warning

Never reprint an existing tag number onto a new label while the original is still attached. The item will be counted twice and the duplicate will be found months later during a reconciliation nobody can explain.

7.7 · Procedures

Linen room procedures

The four procedures below cover a normal shift: receiving a pass, running a batch, delivering, and handing over at the end of the shift.

Procedure — receiving a pass

  1. Open the pass from the station's pass list.
  2. Count the items physically, by type, before scanning anything.
  3. Scan each tag as it is counted. Items without a tag are tagged first, then scanned.
  4. Compare the scanned count with the pass quantity. Where it differs, record a short receipt with the count you found.
  5. Confirm receipt. The pass moves to received and the items become available for batching.
◆78◆
7 · User Manual — Linen Room AppLoveLaundry — System Manual

Procedure — running a wash batch

  1. Create a batch for the machine and load it.
  2. Scan each item into the batch and select start_wash.
  3. At the end of the cycle, select complete_wash for the batch and scan out any item removed for separate treatment.
  4. After pressing, scan each item and select press, then ready when it is racked.

Procedure — delivering from the linen room

Delivery is recorded in the laundry app against the gate pass, not in the linen room. The linen room's part is to ensure that every item on the rack has been scanned to ready, so that the delivery quantity is supported by tag history. Where the linen room is also the dispatch point, scan the items out as deliver at handover so that the tag and the delivery agree.

Note

Shift handover: confirm the batch count on screen matches the physical count, note any open discrepancies, and sign out. An unsigned station is an unattributable one.

7.8 · Troubleshooting

Linen room — troubleshooting

Table 49 — Common problems at the station
SymptomLikely causeAction
Scan produces nothingField lost focus, or scanner in keyboard-wedge mode disconnectedTap the scan field and scan again; check the scanner cable or pairing
“Invalid transition”Item is not in the state the action requiresRead the current status on the card; choose a legal action
“Tag not found”Tag belongs to another laundry, or was never issuedCheck the tag number against the print batch; do not create a duplicate
Item scanned twiceDouble trigger or repeated scanNo action — scans are idempotent for the same action
Batch count does not match the rackItem removed without scanning outScan the item to its actual stage; record an unscanned-item note
Cannot print tagsRole lacks linen:writeAsk a supervisor to print, or to adjust the role

When the network is down

The station cannot record scans without a connection to bill_service. Do not continue scanning into a local file or a paper list and enter it later as if it happened in sequence: the timestamps would be false and the batch history misleading. Record the physical count on paper, keep the items segregated, and enter the scans when the connection returns, noting the delay. Chapter 11.4 describes what remains usable while a service is unavailable.

◆79◆
7 · User Manual — Linen Room AppLoveLaundry — System Manual

Escalation

Escalate to a supervisor when an item cannot be identified, when a discrepancy involves more than a few items, or when a tag appears to exist in two batches. Escalate to the platform operator only when the application itself fails — a blank screen, a repeated server error, or a sign-in that fails for every user.

Note

Report the tag number and the exact message. A screenshot of the station screen is the fastest possible evidence.

7.9 · Linen lifecycle state machine

Linen lifecycle state machine

Seven forward states, three exception states, and no way back.

The scan procedure that writes these transitions is on page 75. The forward path is linear because the physical process is linear: goods are collected, received, washed, finished, pressed, made ready and delivered. Modelling it as a chain rather than a set of flags means an item cannot be simultaneously ready and in wash.

The exception states branch off the active state rather than replacing the chain. An item marked missing leaves the batch but keeps its history, so when it is found it can be scanned back into the correct stage without inventing a new tag.

Rule

There is no reverse transition and no status dropdown. A wrongly scanned item is corrected by recording the event and scanning it forward again, which leaves both facts visible.
